title: The Steadfast Tin Soldier
summary: A one legged tin soldier watches a paper girl and faces many dangers.
coverScene: A brave tin soldier with one leg stands proudly on a wooden table next to a small paper castle.

sentences.text: Once upon a time, from a worn iron spoon cast aside in a dusty workshop, twenty magnificent brothers were born into the world. Their creator had only enough precious metal for that exact number, shaping each infantryman with proud shoulders and a steady gaze. Every single soldier stood straight in his polished uniform, bearing the weight of his duty without a single complaint. The very last of them, however, had been fashioned with only one leg because the molten tin ran out before his mold could be fully satisfied. Although he balanced on a single limb, he stood as firmly and resolutely as the others who possessed a matched pair.

They were placed upon a wooden table amidst a glittering array of discarded playthings and forgotten treasures. Beside them stood a wonderful paper castle with tiny glass windows reflecting the morning light, and near its gates lingered a lovely little paper dancer. She wore a skirt of gossamer gauze and a narrow blue ribbon across her shoulder, pinned with a sparkling sequin. The dancer stood entirely on one leg, extending her other limb backward so high that the observant metal soldier could not see it at all. This elegant posture made the lonely tin soldier think that she was just like him, bearing her singular balance with grace.

He watched her across the varnished wood all day long, wishing to make her his wife, though he dared not speak his mind aloud. Not once did he regret his missing limb, for he felt that they shared a silent understanding that transcended ordinary speech. When night descended upon the quiet room, the toys were freed from their boxes to play at housekeeping and war. A small, black toy enemy that sat snugly inside a painted wooden box suddenly became intensely jealous of the soldier. The dark jack-in-the-box told him sharply to look away from the dancer and mind his own station.

The soldier pretended that he did not hear the warning, keeping his gaze fixed firmly on the delicate lady of paper. The goblin grinned maliciously and hissed that the morning would bring a reckoning for such stubborn disregard of authority. The next morning, as the first pale rays of dawn filtered through the dusty panes, the poor soldier fell down from the window. Whether the malicious goblin pushed him or the autumn wind caught his heavy base remains a mystery, but he tumbled straight onto the cobblestone street below.

The descent was swift and terrifying, landing the soldier headfirst between the paving stones with his bayonet stuck firmly in the mud. Two young boys, running past in the damp morning air, found him immediately and paused to inspect their prize. They placed him carefully into a small paper boat folded from a discarded newspaper and pushed him out into the gutter. The street had become a rushing river from the overnight rain, and the frail vessel sailed down a dark water pipe with alarming speed.

Darkness closed in around the little traveler as the paper walls began to soften under the relentless assault of the swirling current. A large water rat that lived beneath the wooden planks of the drain suddenly demanded to see a pass. Because the soldier had no passport or official papers to show, the terrified boat rushed faster into a wide water path. The dirty water covered him completely, threatening to sweep him away into the murky depths of the underground pipes.

Suddenly, a large and hungry fish swam up from the shadows and took the soldier whole in the dark water. Inside the belly of the beast, it was pitch black and terribly cramped, yet the soldier never dropped his rifle. After some time had passed in that suffocating darkness, a fisherman caught the creature in a great net and took it to the busy market. A cook bought the fish for the midday meal and carried it back to the warm kitchen with a heavy basket.

When the cook cut the fish open with a sharp knife, she was astonished to find the soldier inside the glistening belly. She picked him up by his belt with two fingers and carried him back to the very same room where he had lived before. The soldier was remarkably unchanged by his ordeal, save for a slight tarnish on his bright red coat. He was exceedingly happy to see his lovely paper dancer standing once again in her familiar place by the castle.

Suddenly, without any warning, a small child picked up the metal soldier and threw him straight into the warm fire of the tiled stove. The child gave no reason for the cruel act, acting out of a sudden, careless impulse. A strong draft rushed through the room and blew the paper dancer off her platform and into the fire too. They burned together in the flickering flames until nothing remained of their paper and paint except a small heart made of solid metal.

The fire burned very hot, fed by dry pine logs that crackled and spat sparks into the dark hearth. The room was filled with a bright, blinding light as the intense heat melted the tin soldier down to a shapeless lump. Yet the small heart remained intact where the fire had been the fiercest, glowing with a soft, enduring warmth. People who later cleared the cold ashes and saw the metal heart knew that the strange story was true.

The metal heart stayed there upon the iron grate for a long time, untouched by the sweeping brush or the gathering dust. Every person who entered the room could see the small heart resting among the gray cinders. The memory of the steadfast soldier and the graceful dancer lived on in the hearts of those who looked upon it. Their enduring love proved to be stronger than the fire itself, surviving every trial the world could invent.

Nothing could ever change what they felt for each other through all the trials of their brief existence. The end of the story came with a quiet peace that settled over the silent, shadowy room. The little metal heart rested softly in the ashes, carrying the quiet proof of a devotion that defied the flames.
